summary: Four verified previews cover the EU-Indonesia trade signing, further Hormuz tanker reports, quantified EU budget and digital-tax proposals, and Qatar-Tehran talks. Two follow-ups connect to retained v1 history. Full-detail publication remains held.
limitations: Partial targeted report for 21 November 20:15:00 to 22 November 00:28:50 SGT, completed 00:31:37. Discovery overlap began at 20:00 on 21 November. This does not establish exhaustive Reuters wire coverage or fill earlier missing editions and retrieval gaps. The last complete source-scan cutoff remains unestablished.

All four source developments are represented as metadata previews: two initial versions and two connected follow-ups. Hormuz v2 retains the Friday fire v1 and adds Saturday reports; it does not assert two distinct vessels. EU budget v2 retains France's earlier objection and adds quantified proposals. Existing unrelated held version chains, including Anthropic, are unchanged.

Selected facts were independently checked in Reuters-attributed reporting. Original 21 November publication dates are verified, but accessible publication/update clocks differ from the source-register minute labels. Exact publication, revision and development timestamps remain null. The Qatar visit occurred Friday night, 20 November, so this newly reviewed report is conservatively marked catch-up; the source had labelled its Saturday disclosure in-window.

Trade signing is not entry into force; early-2027 implementation and EUR650m annual savings are expectations. The budget and 3% digital levy are proposals, not enacted law. EUR40bn and EUR180.6bn reductions use different baselines. Tanker accounts and Iran's mine claim remain unresolved. Diplomatic talks do not establish a ceasefire or reopened shipping route. No attributable market reaction or executable FX/security quote is supplied.

These are metadata previews only. stories.topic: EUROPEAN UNION / INDONESIA / ASEAN / TRADE / TARIFFS
stories.headline: EU and Indonesia sign trade agreements; implementation still requires approval
stories.body: Reuters reported that the EU and Indonesia signed comprehensive trade and investment-protection agreements after ten years of negotiations. Planned tariff removal covers more than 90% of products, including EU vehicles facing Indonesian duties as high as 50%. Estimated annual duty savings for EU exporters are EUR650m. Negotiations initially concluded in September 2025; European Parliament consent and internal procedures remain before expected early-2027 implementation. Signing is distinct from entry into force, and estimated tariff savings are not realised corporate profit. No directly attributable equity, bond or currency reaction was verified.
stories.analysis: Trade diversification could support exporters and regional supply chains while increasing competition; realised benefits depend on ratification and implementation.
stories.watch_next: European Parliament consent, Indonesian approvals and the final effective date.

stories.topic: GULF / OMAN / STRAIT OF HORMUZ / OIL / SHIPPING / INSURANCE
stories.headline: Saturday tanker reports extend the retained Hormuz shipping-security story
stories.body: Reuters reported UKMTO accounts of a Saturday tanker stern strike 11 nautical miles north of Khasab and an engine-room strike 17 nautical miles east. Whether the two reports concern the same vessel was unresolved. No casualties were reported; environmental effects remained unknown. Iran separately claimed a mine strike, which Reuters could neither independently verify nor link to a specific UKMTO incident. These Saturday reports extend the retained Friday fire story, without establishing a new production outage or another confirmed waterway closure. No incident-specific oil-price move was verified.
stories.analysis: Further incidents add uncertainty for shipping, insurance and energy logistics; reported attacks and measured supply losses remain different facts.
stories.watch_next: Vessel identities, confirmed damage, maritime notices and tanker movements.
stories.earlier: Retained v1 covered the separate 20 November tanker fire eight nautical miles north of Khasab and competing projectile/mine accounts. This v2 adds Saturday reports at different locations; it does not revise the earlier event into a new vessel count.

stories.topic: EUROPEAN UNION / FRANCE / ANTONIO COSTA / FISCAL POLICY / TECHNOLOGY / DIGITAL TAX
stories.headline: EU budget follow-up adds proposed EUR40bn reduction and 3% digital levy
stories.body: Reuters detailed Antonio Costa's proposed 2028-2034 budget of EUR1.582tn: EUR40bn below October's draft and EUR180.6bn below the initial Commission plan. These use different baselines. A proposed 3% levy on qualifying digital advertising, intermediation and user-data turnover has potential equity implications for Google (Alphabet), Microsoft, Meta Platforms, Apple Inc. and Amazon. Leaders plan talks on 26-27 November and seek agreement in December. Unanimous agreement remains necessary; neither the budget nor tax is approved. No attributable euro, Bund or technology-share reaction was verified.
stories.analysis: The proposed budget path and digital-tax exposure could affect future investment and technology profitability, subject to the final design and approval.
stories.watch_next: The 26-27 November summit, levy scope and unanimous agreement.
stories.earlier: Retained v1 described France's objection to the EU budget draft over agricultural income support. This v2 adds quantified budget comparisons and a digital-tax proposal, while preserving the earlier objection and its date.

stories.topic: QATAR / IRAN / GULF / DIPLOMACY / ENERGY / MARITIME SECURITY
stories.headline: Iranian official reports Qatar delegation talks in Tehran; no agreement established
stories.body: Reuters reported an Iranian deputy foreign minister's account of a delegation from Qatar holding talks in Tehran on Friday night, 20 November. He said mediator contacts continued in person and virtually. The Saturday report is a newly reviewed disclosure about an earlier meeting; its precise event time is unverified. Diplomatic contact does not establish a signed settlement or confirmed reopening of shipping routes. No directly attributable oil, FX or bond-market response was verified.
stories.analysis: The meeting provides a potential diplomatic channel during regional shipping concerns; significance depends on subsequent verifiable commitments.
stories.watch_next: Joint statements, formal proposals and confirmed shipping conditions.
